kartice.naslov: Fragmented landscapes of mobile transposable element families bolster the diversity of large-effect alleles in Arabidopsis
kartice.povzetek_sl: Transposable elements (TEs) are powerful endogenous mutagens, but our understanding of the 'mobilome' - the set of mobile TEs at the species level - has largely been shaped by the study of a single reference genome. To overcome this reference-centric view, we produced long-read genome assemblies for 91 Arabidopsis thaliana strains and performed a reference-free pangenomic graph analysis of structural variants. Our analysis revealed the presence of twice as many TE families with recent mobilization activity as previously described. These >200 newly identified TE families are ancestral, with a third experimentally shown to be mobile and although they are often characterized by the presence of full-length copies in only a few rather than in most strains, they nonetheless contribute significantly to the generation of large-effect alleles. These findings uncover a much more fragmented and impactful mobilome than previously documented and highlight how pangenome approaches dramatically improve the study of genetic diversity.

kartice.naslov: History of opioid use disorder correlates with altered neuroimmune signatures in the human dorsal root ganglia
kartice.povzetek_sl: Understanding mechanisms for the negative reinforcing effects of opioids are fundamental to improving patient care. Using human dorsal root ganglia (DRG) from donors with and without opioid use disorder (OUD), we set out to examine functional and molecular correlates of chronic opioid use. At a molecular level, we detected disrupted immune signatures throughout cells in the peripheral nervous system (PNS), spanning glial-neuroimmune interactions to changes in non-neuronal senescence. At the physiological level these changes are paired with sensitization of DRG sensory neurons. Our findings reveal a neuro-inflammatory state in the PNS of individuals with OUD. Targeting therapeutics towards these PNS-based mechanisms could be an approach to alleviating the negative reinforcing effects of opioids.

kartice.povzetek_sl: Passive acoustic monitoring often summarizes long recordings as fixed-window presence predictions, but many ecological questions require records of individual vocal events: how many occurred, when they occurred, whether they overlapped, how long they lasted, what frequency band they occupied, and whether each event was complete enough for structural measurement. We address this event-level measurement problem with SpectroBird, a spectrogram-based method for localizing and curating avian vocalizations in noisy field recordings. SpectroBird first applies a detection-localization model to identify candidate vocalizations as time-frequency boxes. kartice.naslov: SLAFIT: Viral fitness inference and structural variant detection from TGS data
kartice.povzetek_sl: Evolution is driven by genetic variation at multiple scales, from single-nucleotide variants (SNVs) to structural variants (SVs). Within populations, nonrandom associations among SNVs, quantified by linkage disequilibrium (LD), must be considered when inferring fitness from sequencing data. Characterizing SVs, SNVs, and the LD between SNVs therefore provides complementary insights into the genetic basis of evolutionary change. Although third-generation sequencing technologies facilitate the characterization of genomic variation, finite read lengths often limit the resolution of LD across entire genomes. Here, we present SLAFIT, a pipeline for linkage-aware fitness inference and SV detection from third-generation sequencing data. The pipeline reconstructs genome-wide haplotypes and their frequencies from third-generation sequencing reads to infer SNVs and estimate LD. kartice.naslov: The (implicit) force is with you: an application of the implicit function theorem for automatic protein force fields reparametrization
kartice.povzetek_sl: Molecular dynamics simulations are powerful tools for studying protein behavior, yet their accuracy remains limited by the approximations of molecular force fields and the difficulty of determining their parameters. Moreover, existing force fields are largely optimized for globular proteins and can perform poorly on structurally distinct systems. Developing a universal force field that accurately describes all existing protein structures may be beyond reach with current physical models. Instead, we propose shifting generality from the force field itself to the method used to assign its parameters, enabling systematic reparameterization for restricted, structurally homogeneous classes of proteins. We formulate this task as a bilevel optimization problem and solve it using the implicit function theorem. We demonstrate this approach by reparameterizing AMBER for amyloid fibrils, optimizing its parameters to improve agreement with experimentally determined structures and enhance fibril stability during molecular dynamics simulations.
